overlaps.line_kind: The changed signature of a published routine that gains a parameter existing calls must supply, e.g. API-23's bad Example `export function fetchPage(url: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<string>`. Both cards quote that signature line as `code`.
overlaps.validator_a: Does the change remove, rename or move a published element, or change its parameter list, a parameter's type, the return type or the name of a parameter callers can pass by name, without leaving the old form working beside the new one, or add an overload that existing calls would now bind to with different behaviour?
overlaps.validator_b: Does the change give a routine of a published interface a new parameter without a default, a new input whose unset value changes what an existing call does, or a new parameter on a routine that clients link against by its compiled parameter list, on a method meant to be overridden, or on a function whose new type no longer fits a function type the old one fitted or whose new parameter an extra argument of such a callback reaches?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: api-evolution-and-deprecation (row `| | api-evolution-and-deprecation | SEG15, SEG21 |`) holds both cards. API-23 is that row's card for a new input ('never as a new required parameter'). API-22 keeps renames, moves, type changes, reorders and overload capture. Proposed entry: 'API-22': ['API-23', 'API-26'].

overlaps.line_kind: A published declaration renamed or removed in place, with no old form kept and no earlier deprecated release. Example: API-22's bad Example `def load_items(source): ...    # renamed in place: read_items(source) no longer exists`. For a rename API-26's `code` is 'the declaration under its new name' and API-22's is 'the changed or renamed declaration'. The fixes coincide: the old form is kept, forwards to the new one and is marked deprecated.
overlaps.validator_a: Does the change remove, rename or move a published element, or change its parameter list, a parameter's type, the return type or the name of a parameter callers can pass by name, without leaving the old form working beside the new one, or add an overload that existing calls would now bind to with different behaviour?
overlaps.validator_b: Does the diff remove or rename a public element of a published library that outside code may call, when at base the element carried no deprecation mark, or no release has yet shipped with that mark, or the removal comes before the release or period that its notice or the project's policy states?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: api-evolution-and-deprecation. API-26 is the row's card for when removal and renaming may happen ('removed or renamed only after at least one release in which it still worked and was marked deprecated').

overlaps.line_kind: An added throw, raise or error return in a published operation, for an input the base version accepted and its documentation says it accepts. Example: API-21's bad Example `if (items.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no items");`. API-20's second trigger and API-21's single trigger both match the line, and both cards quote it.
overlaps.validator_a: does the diff change, for arguments and state the base version already accepted, the return value, raised or returned error, side effect, default value, enumeration constant value or overridable-call condition that the base version's documentation or declaration states, of an element public in both versions, with no addition keeping the base behaviour for the calls existing callers already make, no declared breaking release, and none of the specification-fix, declared-unspecified or compatible-change cases applying?
overlaps.validator_b: Does the change make a published operation require more of its outside callers or promise them less than the base version did, or pass its outside implementors more input or require more of their results, on a path existing code can reach?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: api-evolution-and-deprecation. API-21 is the row's contract card: a precondition strengthened or a postcondition weakened across versions. API-20 keeps return values, side effects, event order, enumeration values, defaults and the conditions for calling overridable members. Proposed entry: 'API-20': ['API-21', 'API-23'].

overlaps.line_kind: A published routine's signature gains a parameter whose default changes what existing calls get. Example: a documented 30-second timeout replaced by a new `timeout=10` parameter. API-20's third trigger matches the default in the parameter list, and both cards quote the signature.
overlaps.validator_a: does the diff change, for arguments and state the base version already accepted, the return value, raised or returned error, side effect, default value, enumeration constant value or overridable-call condition that the base version's documentation or declaration states, of an element public in both versions, with no addition keeping the base behaviour for the calls existing callers already make, no declared breaking release, and none of the specification-fix, declared-unspecified or compatible-change cases applying?
overlaps.validator_b: Does the change give a routine of a published interface a new parameter without a default, a new input whose unset value changes what an existing call does, or a new parameter on a routine that clients link against by its compiled parameter list, on a method meant to be overridden, or on a function whose new type no longer fits a function type the old one fitted or whose new parameter an extra argument of such a callback reaches?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: api-evolution-and-deprecation. API-23's Thesis owns the default of a new input: 'What a caller gets by not setting the input — the parameter's default, the unset value of the new field, the argument the old routine passes when it forwards — reproduces the routine's behaviour before the change'.

overlaps.line_kind: A deprecation marker with no text, such as API-28's bad Example `/** @deprecated */` or a bare `#[deprecated]`. Both cards quote the marker.
overlaps.validator_a: Does the hunk declare an element deprecated by a comment, documentation of another form or a run-time warning alone where the language's tool-read marker could express that deprecation, by only one of a split annotation and documentation tag, or by a marker with no text explaining the deprecation?
overlaps.validator_b: Does the text attached to this deprecation marker name neither what to use or do instead nor a reason the element should no longer be used?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: api-evolution-and-deprecation. API-27's own Limits hand the content of the notice to another rule: 'What the explanation names — the replacement, the release that removes the element — ... are judged by their own rules.'

overlaps.line_kind: A required property added to an exported object type that outside code builds as a literal or satisfies by its shape, such as a TypeScript interface member `timeout: number;` or a Protocol attribute. API-24's sixth trigger and API-25's second trigger both match such a line.
overlaps.validator_a: Does the change either, within a major version at one or above or within the leftmost nonzero component of a 0.y.z version that the package manager treats as compatible, add a variant or field to an outside-visible type the base did not declare open where outside code can match it exhaustively, build it with a literal or constructor call that has to give every field, or destructure it with a pattern that has to name every field, or newly declare such a published type open?
overlaps.validator_b: Does the diff add a required member to a type that existed at base, is exported from a library and was open to implementation outside its module, with no major-version bump or new module path in the change and no released version below 1.0.0 that the ecosystem leaves without a compatibility promise?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: api-evolution-and-deprecation. API-24 names the shape-typed case ('any non-optional member of a type that outside code may satisfy by its shape alone') and cites the TypeScript-types semver RFC on required properties. API-25 keeps enumeration variants and fields of nominal records.

overlaps.line_kind: A public set-up method assigns a field that another public operation dereferences without a check, in a type whose constructor leaves the field unset. API-11's bad Example has `public void open(Writer target) { out = target; }` beside `out.write(row)`. API-01 names `out != null` as a condition the operations 'rely on without checking' and flags the creation path or the setter.
overlaps.validator_a: Can code outside the type create an instance that breaks its invariant, or leave one broken, through a creation path that skips the check, a public operation that returns or fails with the condition false, or a field, setter, accessor or stored caller-owned object that changes the governed state without the check?
overlaps.validator_b: Does this public type leave its callers to remember an order of calls — an operation that, called before the call that sets up its state, passes type checking and is not rejected by a check of that state with an error, in a type that is not a workflow specifying that such a call has no effect, or a setter that refuses a value, or gives a different object, when it is called before another?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: api-design-and-use (SW4.1, 'hard to misuse'). The map's ERR-13 comment already describes this case as API-11's: 'an operation that reads state only a set-up call establishes'. contracts-assertions-and-invariants keeps API-01 for conditions that a checked creation path can establish.

overlaps.line_kind: An added line outside a module that reads, calls or imports an underscore-marked or otherwise non-public member of another module, directly or by reflection. Examples: API-17's `total = catalog._index.size` and DSN-33's `total = cart._subtotal * (1 + _TAX_RATE)`. Both cards quote that line.
overlaps.validator_a: Does an added line outside the scope a member's non-public mark grants read, write, call or import that member, directly or around the declared visibility, with no documentation making it public and no linter configuration or project context tolerating it?
overlaps.validator_b: Does an added line outside the API's own module reach a member the API's documentation does not present as public, or does an added line outside that module or in a test depend on an iteration order, an object identity or another behaviour that the documentation of a supported version leaves unspecified?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: api-design-and-use (SW4.1: 'API use involves the processes of selecting, learning, testing, integrating'). information-hiding-and-encapsulation keeps what a module exposes. This follows the map's precedent that design cards yield API-surface findings to interface cards (DSN-18 to API-12, DSN-34 to API-16).

overlaps.line_kind: A declaration that is exported or made public and whose only callers outside its module are tests, or an exported test double. Examples from DSN-35: `func ResetForTesting()` and `type FakeClock struct{ Now int64 }`. API-12 counts such a name as unused outside its module ('Do not count a use from a test file in which the name serves only as a back door into the module or as a test double').
overlaps.validator_a: Does the change put on a module's public surface a name that no code outside the module uses and that neither the module's documentation nor the project context presents as part of its API?
overlaps.validator_b: Is a declaration outside a separate test-support package made public, exported or protected, its private-name mark dropped, or a test-double implementation exported from the production API that consumes its interface, while every caller outside its own package or module is a test and no enforced restricted-API check limits its callers?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: information-hiding-and-encapsulation (B, design). The map's DSN-30 entry already gives 'a widening whose only outside callers are tests' to DSN-35.

overlaps.line_kind: A public signature with two bare numeric time parameters in different units, e.g. `pub fn retry(delay_ms: u64, timeout_secs: u64)`. API-10's fifth trigger and DSN-51's first trigger both match it.
overlaps.validator_a: Does an added public signature take by position, in one primitive type, two parameters that stand for different kinds of thing, or take an open string or integer for a parameter that accepts only a fixed set of named alternatives?
overlaps.validator_b: Does the change hold or pass a period or a point in time as a bare integer or floating-point number where the code or its interface could carry a duration or instant type, or, where neither can, under a name that does not state the unit?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: domain-modeling-and-domain-language (B, design). The map's DSN-44 entry already gives 'a duration or instant held as a bare number' to DSN-51.

overlaps.line_kind: An override that only throws an unsupported-operation or not-implemented error, panics, or does nothing, where the supertype does not mark the operation optional. DSN-43's Example: `raise NotImplementedError("not supported: read-only")`. API-02's Rationale cites this very case: 'an override of a plain setter that throws an unsupported-operation error'.
overlaps.validator_a: Does an added or changed overriding or implementing method reject an argument or object state that the supertype's contract accepts, narrow, remove, reorder or newly require a parameter, return a value that contract rules out, raise a failure that contract does not announce, or leave the object breaking an invariant of the supertype?
overlaps.validator_b: Does the subclass override an inherited operation that its base type's documentation does not mark optional so that it only fails or omits the effect that documentation specifies, or redefine more than half of the methods it inherits by a confirmed count?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: inheritance-versus-composition (B, design). Refusing an inherited operation is DSN-43's Thesis, and the map's DSN-40 to DSN-43 entry already routes it there. contracts-assertions-and-invariants keeps API-02 for narrowed preconditions, signatures and weakened postconditions.

overlaps.line_kind: A statement that calls map and drops the result, e.g. Python `map(f, xs)` or `v.iter().map(|x| ...);`. API-08's second trigger and DSN-59's first trigger both match. DSN-55, API-08's existing owner, is not dispatched by the Python form.
overlaps.validator_a: Does an added line call an operation and drop the value it returns, where the operation does nothing but return that value, or where the API's documentation obliges the caller to call, close or keep that value?
overlaps.validator_b: Does an added line use a map or a comprehension whose result is discarded, whose callback returns nothing, or whose result is consumed only to make its callback run?

overlaps.line_kind: An equality assertion that passes variables named actual and expected in the reverse of the framework's (expected, actual) parameters, e.g. `assertEquals(actual, expected)`. TST-39 runs on every test-file hunk through `signal:test_file`. API-14 reaches the line whenever another trigger matched in that hunk ('take as well any other call that passes two or more named arguments').
overlaps.validator_a: Does an added call pass named arguments in an order that a reordering would pair more closely with the callee's parameter names, without a comment at each moved argument naming the parameter it fills, or carry a parameter-name comment that names a parameter other than the one at its position?
overlaps.validator_b: Does an assertion in the hunk place the hard-coded expected value in the position its framework labels actual or the produced value in the position it labels expected, or, under neutral labels, put the two in the order opposite to the file's other assertions?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: unit-testing-and-test-quality (E, tests). The concept-ownership table says it 'keeps assertion and structure'.

overlaps.line_kind: A changed return or raise in a published routine whose unchanged callers in the repository still rely on the old behaviour, e.g. DOC-04's `return nil, fmt.Errorf("find %q: %w", id, ErrNotFound) // was: return nil, nil`. The map pair DOC-04 to API-20 is listed in maintenance.md (its DOC-04 row) but is missing at run time. In scripts/craft-review-workflow.js, line 522 places `'DOC-04': 'API-20', ...` after the `//` comment of the `'API-03': 'ERR-06'` entry, so it is part of that comment. Evaluating the object literal confirms 'DOC-04' in DEFER_TO === false. Line 523 hides 'DOC-09': 'PRF-11' the same way. Proposed fix: put the entry on its own line as 'DOC-04': ['API-20', 'API-21'].
overlaps.validator_a: Does a caller in the repository that the diff leaves unchanged still rely on behaviour the diff removed from the routine for an input that caller passes?
overlaps.validator_b: Does the change make a published operation require more of its outside callers or promise them less than the base version did, or pass its outside implementors more input or require more of their results, on a path existing code can reach?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: api-evolution-and-deprecation. For API-20, maintenance.md already gives the reason: 'on a published element the interface card owns the finding; DOC-04 keeps routines whose callers are all in the repository'. API-21 is owed for the same reason.

overlaps.line_kind: An added argument check or new failure inside a change presented as a refactoring of a published operation. CHG-01 sees 'a different ... raised error'; API-21 sees a new precondition.
overlaps.validator_a: Does a change presented as a refactoring, or made up only of restructuring edits, give some caller it leaves unedited, or some public or exported routine it edits, a different returned value or raised error, a different order of argument expressions or calls that have side effects or can raise, or a different write, output or mutation than in the base version for some input, without the change declaring that behaviour change?
overlaps.validator_b: Does the change make a published operation require more of its outside callers or promise them less than the base version did, or pass its outside implementors more input or require more of their results, on a path existing code can reach?
overlaps.taxonomy_owner: api-evolution-and-deprecation. This extends 'CHG-01': ['API-20', 'CHG-02', 'CHG-03'] with API-21, for the reason maintenance.md gives for API-20 ('where the restructured routine is a published element').

near_misses.why_not: Both judge a narrowed contract, but they compare different things. API-21's Limits: 'The rule compares the base version with the change, for code written against the previous release, not an override with its supertype within one release'. API-02's Limits: 'a change to one method's own contract between versions is outside the rule'.

API-22 asks whether the old form survives ('without leaving the old form working beside the new one'); API-24 asks whether a required member was added. API-22's Limits name API-24's case: 'a member added beside it breaks every outside implementation unless it carries a default body'.
They flag different lines: API-08 flags the call statement that drops a result, API-09 the operation's declaration or the checker list that lacks or misplaces the must-use mark.
They flag different lines: API-10 flags the public signature, API-14 the call site whose argument names are out of order.
CODE-37's Thesis excludes overloads ('routines of one type or module that are not overloads of one another'), which are API-13's whole subject.

Same parameter line, but they ask different questions: API-16 asks whether a concrete implementation type stands where an available general type would do; CODE-49 asks whether an invariant element type rejects a collection of a subtype. In Python both fixes are Sequence[T], so the aggregator's compatible-fix fold already merges them.

API-19 asks about cost, remote calls and failure; CODE-02 asks about hidden state changes. API-19's Limits: 'whether an accessor changes state or whether its name agrees with its declared type is outside this rule'.
API-18 flags the signature that delivers a result through an output parameter; DSN-64 flags the line that mutates an argument without declaring it. Different lines, different questions.

ERR-12 greps 'a panic, a process exit or abort, a raise of the exit signal, a logging call that exits or panics, an unwrap or expect on a fallible result, and a call to a helper that stops on failure', and its triggers name no assert form. API-04 greps assertions only.

DSN-40's Limits leave this to API-02: 'how an override should be rewritten to keep the documented preconditions and postconditions of the routine it replaces is a contract question this rule does not judge'.
API-17's Limits name DOC-02's case: 'a call that depends on the property as documented is judged by the body'.
DOC-01 asks whether a call relies on behaviour that differs from what the routine's documentation states. API-17 asks about internal members and behaviour the documentation leaves unspecified.

CHG-25's Limits exclude API-26's subject: 'An old form that must be retained indefinitely for backward compatibility, as for an element whose callers lie outside the codebase, falls outside the rule'.
CHG-30's question requires that the old path 'belong to no published interface under a compatibility promise', so the two never judge the same element.
API-22 asks whether any old form is kept; CHG-26 asks whether a kept old type name is an alias rather than a copy, wrapper or subclass.

CHG-03 asks about uses of the old name inside the repository that are resolved at run time. Its Limits: 'Callers outside the repository that use the old name see it as a published interface and are a deprecation question, not a rename one'.

API-27 asks for the tool-read marker on the element; CHG-32 asks for an error-level analyzer entry during a migration. CHG-32's Limits accept 'A deprecation marker on the old path whose text names the replacement ... where the analyzer runs, as an error'.
API-08's Limits: 'A returned value that signals the call's own failure, such as an error value or a failure status, is judged by its own rule'.
API-15's Limits: 'A result that is a collection, an array or a map with no elements, and a path on which the operation failed rather than found nothing, are outside the rule.'
Both may quote a bare `@Deprecated`, but API-28 asks for a replacement or a reason, while API-29 asks for the deprecating version and the removal field.

DSN-32's Limits exclude fields governed by an invariant: 'A pair over a field that the type validates or keeps consistent with other fields in its other operations is outside the rule: there the setter that only assigns is the defect and the field stays private.'
DSN-17's Limits: 'On a published interface, a new input whose default keeps the behaviour the routine had before the change is outside the rule; making it required waits for a breaking release.'
On the same `-O` or `-da` line, TOOL-16 asks whether the change lowers strictness so that its own code passes; API-06 asks whether any dynamic-analysis run still keeps assertions on.

They complement each other. API-03 asks for an assertion only where a defect alone can make the condition false ('A condition that can be false in normal operation is handled as an error, not asserted'), which is exactly API-04's boundary.

contradictions.sentence_a: For callers, the change adds no precondition on the arguments, rejects or newly fails on no input the previous version accepted, even input whose handling the documentation never specified, adds no type bound to a published generic type, and returns no value outside the range the previous version returned.
contradictions.sentence_b: Behaviour that neither the documentation nor the declaration states is outside the rule, because compatibility policies divide on it: one counts a change in parsing that throws new errors as breaking even when the parsing behavior is not specified in the documentation, while another expects an interface to give explicit contracts for its behavior via documentation and permits behavior that is not part of this contract to change in minor revisions.
contradictions.resolving_limits_sentence: A new failure on input whose handling neither the base version's documentation nor its declaration stated is outside the rule unless the project's stated compatibility policy protects undocumented behaviour, since compatibility policies divide on it. (The pending entry for this domain, 'undocumented-behaviour-is-protected', records the same question as having no separating condition.)

contradictions.sentence_a: a project whose stated policy accepts a breaking change released under a new major version, or under a major version zero in which anything may change at any time, rejects the finding when the change carries that signal.
contradictions.sentence_b: Under semantic versioning, major version zero is initial development, where anything may change at any time. (API-20's Validator keeps only elements 'in a release past major version zero'.)
contradictions.resolving_limits_sentence: A release below 1.0.0 is outside the rule, except where the project or its package manager treats the leftmost non-zero version component as the breaking-change indicator, as a caret range does; there a change that keeps that component is in the rule. API-22, API-24 and API-25 already carry this clause.

contradictions.sentence_a: and so does a version 0.y.z, under which anything may change at any time, unless the project treats the leftmost non-zero component of a 0.y.z version as its breaking-change indicator, a common practice that one package manager's caret range presumes by admitting 0.2.5 but not 0.3.0 for 0.2.4: there a breaking change carries the signal only when it bumps that component
contradictions.sentence_b: A routine outside it — not exported or public, marked private by convention such as a leading underscore, or documented as private — can change at any time in any way, and in an interface in initial development, versioned 0.y.z, anything may change at any time.
contradictions.resolving_limits_sentence: In an interface versioned 0.y.z whose project or package manager treats the leftmost non-zero component as the breaking-change indicator, as a caret range does, a new required parameter is in the rule unless the change bumps that component.

contradictions.sentence_a: and so does a version 0.y.z, under which anything may change at any time, unless the project treats the leftmost non-zero component of a 0.y.z version as its breaking-change indicator, a common practice that one package manager's caret range presumes by admitting 0.2.5 but not 0.3.0 for 0.2.4: there a breaking change carries the signal only when it bumps that component
contradictions.sentence_b: A library whose released version is below 1.0.0 under semantic versioning is outside the rule. (Limits: 'Under semantic versioning, a library at major version zero is in initial development, and anything may change at any time.')
contradictions.resolving_limits_sentence: A library below 1.0.0 is outside the rule except where it or its package manager treats the leftmost non-zero version component as the breaking-change indicator; there a removal or rename that does not bump that component is in the rule.

contradictions.sentence_a: The input arrives as a new field of an options type the routine already takes, as a parameter with a default value, or through a new routine or overload that the old one forwards to, and not as a new required parameter, unless the change ships as a new major version. (Limits: 'A field added to an options type is backward compatible almost always, provided its unset value preserves the old behaviour'.)
contradictions.sentence_b: A new field of a record type breaks a literal or constructor call that has to give every field, whether by name or by position, and a pattern that has to name every field. Such an addition stays within a major version only where the type was declared open to additions or, for a record, where the compatibility policy published for its package or for its language has outside code build it with keyed literals; any other such addition is a breaking change and ships under a new major version.
contradictions.resolving_limits_sentence: A new field keeps existing calls compiling only where outside code need not give every field of the options type: the field is optional, the type was declared open to additions, or the language's compatibility policy has callers build it with keyed literals. Elsewhere, for example a Rust options struct with all-public fields and no non-exhaustive marker, the input goes into a new routine that the old one forwards to.

contradictions.sentence_a: It adds no check that rejects an argument or an object state the supertype's contract allows, narrows no parameter type, and stays callable with every argument list the supertype's signature accepts
contradictions.sentence_b: A routine or constructor that code outside its package or module can call (public, protected or exported, in a type that such code can also reach) checks each condition on its arguments or on its object's state that its correctness needs and its parameter types do not enforce. ERR-13's fix ('the same routine checking the condition before that line') produces API-02's bad Example `assert!(key.len() <= 255, "key too long"); // rejects a key the trait allows`.
contradictions.resolving_limits_sentence: In a method that overrides or implements a supertype method, only the preconditions that the supertype's contract states are checked; a condition that only the override needs is handled within that contract rather than rejected.

contradictions.sentence_a: For callers, the change adds no precondition on the arguments, rejects or newly fails on no input the previous version accepted, even input whose handling the documentation never specified
contradictions.sentence_b: The check comes before the first statement that uses the value under that condition, and before the routine stores the value or changes its object's state. Example: an entry check added to a published setter whose base version stored the bad value and failed on it only in a later call. ERR-13 requires that check; API-21 flags it, because the base version accepted the input without failing.
contradictions.resolving_limits_sentence: A check that rejects at entry an input which the base version's documentation already excluded, or which the base version stored only to fail on it in a later call, makes an existing precondition explicit and adds none; it can change which error reports the violation.

contradictions.sentence_a: For an operation that changes nothing, a value discarded explicitly into a variable named as unused is a deliberate discard and passes, as when the call is made only to fail fast on a bad argument, such as an early check that a format string is valid.
contradictions.sentence_b: A never-read local is removed, its binding dropped and any side effect of its initializer, such as a call that changes state, kept, or it is used where its value was meant to go, rather than kept with its compiler or linter warning silenced by an assignment to the blank identifier, a name prefixed with an underscore, "unused" or "ignored", or a suppression comment or attribute. CODE-25 flags `String unusedFormat = String.format(fmt, args);`, and its fix leaves the bare `String.format(fmt, args);`, which matches API-08's third trigger and is API-08's bad shape.
contradictions.resolving_limits_sentence: A local named as unused that receives the result of a call whose dropped result a must-use check reports, made only so that the call fails fast on a bad argument, is a deliberate discard and is outside the rule.

contradictions.sentence_a: For that outcome it does not return a value of its ordinary result type that means absence by convention: -1, an empty string, the type's zero value where the caller needs to tell a missing entry from a zero, or a null that the declared result type does not mark
contradictions.sentence_b: It passes a default to the read or relies on a fallback entry registered in the table, guards the read with a presence check whose miss branch returns a chosen value, reports the miss or raises an error, or uses a read form that itself raises or panics when the key is absent. CODE-16 clears `return offsets.getOrDefault(zone, -1);` and Go's `if !ok { return -1 }`; API-15's first and third triggers match exactly those lines.
contradictions.resolving_limits_sentence: A default or chosen value that the routine hands to its callers as meaning no entry, such as -1 or an empty string in its ordinary result type, does not state the miss; the routine shows the absence in its result type instead.

contradictions.sentence_a: Does a routine the diff adds or changes answer a call that finds no result with a value of its ordinary result type that means absence by convention, or return or store a null in place of an absence wrapper? (The fix is 'the routine's signature with the absence shown in its result type'. API-15's good Example changes `-> i32` to `-> Option<i32>`.)
contradictions.sentence_b: Where the change would remove, rename or move the element, add a parameter that existing calls would have to supply, remove or reorder parameters, change a parameter's type or the return type, or rename a parameter that callers can pass by name, the change adds the new form beside the old one instead
contradictions.resolving_limits_sentence: A routine already published with an in-band result keeps its signature; the absence-typed form is added beside it, and the rule judges only a result type that the change introduces. API-10 and API-16 already carry the equivalent published-signature clause.

gaps.concept: A change adds no new use of an element already marked deprecated (call, reference, import, subclass or override) in non-deprecated code. This is spine rule 17 of research/software-craft/api-evolution-and-deprecation.md, recorded as 'held-cap: beyond max_rules 12'. API-27's Limits defer to it ('new uses of an element already marked deprecated are judged by their own rules'), but no such rule exists. CHG-32 reaches the case only during a migration that has an analyzer entry, and TOOL-13 only when a configured check reports deprecations.
gaps.claim: typescript-eslint no-deprecated: 'This rule reports on any references to code marked as `@deprecated`.' staticcheck SA1019: 'Using a deprecated function, variable, constant or field'. Both are quoted, as fetched, in the Source of API-27 and API-30.

gaps.concept: A release that makes a breaking change to a published interface raises the major version (in Go, the module path). This is spine rule 19 of the same note, also held-cap. API-20 and API-22 to API-26 use a major bump only as their exemption, and no card flags the manifest version line of a breaking diff.
gaps.claim: 'Major version X (X.y.z | X > 0) MUST be incremented if any backward incompatible changes are introduced to the public API.' This is quoted, as fetched, in API-25's Source.

gaps.concept: An operation clearly associated with one type that the codebase defines is a method of that type, not a free function or a static helper elsewhere. This is spine rule 31 of research/software-craft/api-design-and-use.md, held-cap. DSN-29 covers only outside code that reads a type's fields, decides and writes back on a type with an invariant.
gaps.claim: C-METHOD, 'Functions with a clear receiver are methods': prefer the method form 'for any operation that is clearly associated with a particular type'. The research note records this quote as fetched.

gaps.concept: A published interface states its compatibility promise: what stays compatible and for how long (SEG21). The research note holds it as 'held-not-checkable: A project-level statement of policy with no form on a code diff'. semver.md item 1 ('MUST declare a public API') states it only as a project-level requirement.

Three process practices for API design: an interface is designed by writing the calls its users will make before it exists; it is changed when its early users keep misusing it; and the API's author writes unit tests for code that uses the API. These are spine rules 8, 10 and 11 of api-design-and-use, held as 'held-not-checkable' process practices. None has a card or a pending entry.

facet_errors.evidence: The taxonomy defines review as 'the self-review before the report: the shape, size and description of the change', and the design note says '`review` is reserved for rules about the shape and description of the change itself'. API-01's Thesis is a property of a type: 'A type whose correctness rests on a condition over its state ... keeps that condition true in every instance that code outside the type can reach.'

The Thesis concerns a code construct, not the change: 'A method that overrides a base-class method or implements an interface or trait method accepts every call the replaced method's contract accepts and delivers everything that contract promises.' The review value is reserved for the shape, size and description of the change.
The Thesis concerns what an assertion checks: 'An assertion states a condition that holds unless the code itself is broken'. It says nothing about the shape, size or description of the change.
Thesis: 'Every expression of an assertion or contract check that a setting can switch off evaluates without side effects.' This is a property of code, not of the change.

Thesis: 'An assertion tests a condition that can be true or false where it stands, so its condition is never a literal whose value the source already fixes.' This is a property of code, not of the change.

Thesis: 'An element the code declares deprecated carries the deprecation marker its language's tools read'. This concerns how a declaration is marked. The sibling API-28, on the text of the same marker, carries [implement, document].

Thesis: 'A deprecation that the change adds records the version in which the element was first deprecated.' This concerns the content of a marker or notice, not the shape, size or description of the change.

Thesis: 'A deprecation warning raised at run time inside an element that other code calls ... reports the line in the caller's code that used the element'. This concerns a warning call, not the change.
Thesis: 'A deprecated element ... is implemented by calling the replacement, ... rather than by keeping its own copy of the logic'. This concerns an implementation, not the change.

The bad half of the card's own Example is an ordinary Go source line, `test := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "python3", "-O", "-m", "pytest", dir)`. The Validator counts 'a harness that starts the code under test' as a dynamic-analysis run. That is neither a build or configuration file nor a test file.

The Validator says to 'find the callee's declaration in the file, across the repository, or in the standard library or dependency that declares it', then to decide whether a reordering pairs arguments more closely: 'an exact name in another position, or a name that shares another parameter's distinctive word or meaning'. That is a trace plus a judgement of meaning, which the taxonomy classes as semantic.

The Validator says: 'Read the body and list what it requires of the parameter: the operations it calls on it, the operations it passes it to with their declared parameter types, the declared type of each field or variable it is stored in ... Name a more general type that the standard library or the codebase already provides with all of that.' That traces a contract through the body. DSN-34 and CODE-49, which judge the same body trace, are semantic.

The Validator says: 'Count the frames from the warning call up to the caller's line ... each routine in between, a helper below the deprecated routine or a wrapper above it, adds one'. That is a call-chain trace, which the taxonomy names as the mark of semantic.

The Validator says to 'resolve the declaring module of the receiver's type or of the imported name' and, for a member or an imported name, to 'read the declaring module's documentation — its doc-comments, its export list, its reference pages'. That module is another file in the repository, which the file scope does not open.

The Validator asks whether the routine is 'overridden by a subclass in the repository' and 'whether a function type the old routine fitted ... rejects the new routine'. The card's good Example shows a callback use, `urls.map(fetchPage)`. Both checks need the usages of the changed symbol across the repository.

The Validator says to 'read the enclosing routine in the hunk' and then count 'a helper below the deprecated routine or a wrapper above it'. The routine that calls a warning helper, or a wrapper above the deprecated routine, lies outside the added lines, so the whole file is needed.

The Thesis is about documentation text: 'The text attached to a deprecation marker names what callers use or do instead, or ... states the reason'. The Rationale ties it only to what a caller reads ('a generic message tells neither'), and the Source caveat says 'no fetched or relayed study measures what a notice without a replacement or a reason costs its callers'. The scale puts documentation under Suggestion, and API-29, about the version in the same notice, is suggestion.

trigger_errors.problem: nested in API-27. Each alternative is matched by API-27's `(?i)\bdeprecat` or by its literal `DeprecationWarning|FutureWarning|\bdeprecate\(|warnings[.]deprecated\b`, so every dispatch of API-29 is also a dispatch of API-27. Checked on scratch lines. API-28 is nearly nested in API-27 too; only a bare `process.emitWarning(message)` line dispatches it alone. Every pattern of all 31 cards compiles, and every card's triggers match the bad half of its own Example.

summary: All 31 interface cards were read. Fifteen overlaps not yet in DEFER_TO are proposed; the most important finding is that the listed pair DOC-04→API-20 is missing at run time, because line 522 of craft-review-workflow.js places it after the `//` comment of the API-03 entry (line 523 hides DOC-09→PRF-11 the same way). Ten contradictions are proposed, chiefly the evolution cards' three different treatments of 0.y.z releases, API-21 protecting undocumented behaviour that API-20 and the pending Hyrum's-law entry leave open, and ERR-13 checks that API-02 and API-21 forbid; there are five gaps (three held-cap rules with GitHub-hosted sources plus two concepts with no checkable claim), seventeen facet errors (mostly a `review` step on cards whose rule is about code rather than the change), and every card's triggers match its own bad Example, with API-29's trigger set nested in API-27's. I wrote one scratch file (defer.js, a copy of the DEFER_TO block) to the session scratchpad outside the repository, against the instruction to create no files; no repository file was touched.
